structures.description: The rigid bony vault enclosing and shielding the brain and primary sensory apparatus.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Basilar skull fracture signs include Battle sign (retroauricular ecchymosis), raccoon eyes, and CSF rhinorrhea/otorrhea.

structures.description: The strongest and largest bone of the facial skeleton, forming the temporomandibular joint (TMJ).
structures.clinicalRelevance: Mandibular fractures frequently occur in pairs due to ring-like mechanics.

structures.description: Segmented axial pillar of 33 vertebrae guarding the spinal cord.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Herniated nucleus pulposus commonly compresses L4-L5 or L5-S1 nerve roots.

structures.description: Osteocartilaginous conical cage consisting of 12 pairs of ribs, costal cartilages, and sternum.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Flail chest occurs when 3 or more contiguous ribs fracture in two or more places.

structures.description: S-shaped strut bone connecting the axial skeleton to the appendicular skeleton.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Most frequently fractured long bone, classically at junction of middle and lateral thirds.

structures.description: Massive basin-like bone complex formed by two hip bones and sacrum.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Open-book pelvic fractures risk rapid retroperitoneal hemorrhage.

structures.description: The longest, heaviest, and strongest tubular bone in the human body.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Subcapital femoral neck fractures disrupt retinacular vessels causing avascular necrosis.

structures.description: Powerful triangular multipennate muscle capping the shoulder glenohumeral joint.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Susceptible to denervation atrophy following anterior glenohumeral shoulder dislocation.

structures.description: Thick, fan-shaped muscle forming the anterior axillary fold.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Avulsion of pectoralis tendon typically occurs during heavy bench pressing.

structures.description: Two-headed anterior compartment arm muscle crossing glenohumeral and elbow joints.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Rupture of long head of biceps tendon causes Popeye muscle deformity.

structures.description: Paired strap muscle segmented by transverse tendinous intersections.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Diastasis recti involves stretching and thinning of linea alba.

structures.description: Broadest muscle of the back creating the posterior axillary fold.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Workhorse myocutaneous flap in reconstructive breast surgery.

structures.description: Massive four-bellied anterior thigh muscle group extending the knee.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Tested via the patellar tendon reflex (L3-L4 arc).

structures.description: Muscular four-chambered pump situated in middle mediastinum.
structures.clinicalRelevance: LAD occlusion precipitates anterior STEMI and cardiogenic shock.

structures.description: Paired spongy respiratory viscera executing alveolar gas exchange.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Tension pneumothorax produces contralateral mediastinal shift and obstructive shock.

structures.description: Largest internal metabolic organ performing detoxification and bile synthesis.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Portal hypertension prompts life-threatening esophageal varices.

structures.description: J-shaped muscular digestive reservoir mediating acid digestion.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Parietal cell loss causes intrinsic factor deficiency and Pernicious Anemia.

structures.description: Bean-shaped organs filtering plasma and regulating blood pressure via RAAS.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Renal artery stenosis triggers refractory renovascular hypertension.

structures.description: Cylindrical neural cable extending from medulla to conus medullaris.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Anterior spinal artery syndrome produces motor paralysis below lesion.

structures.description: Primary elastic systemic conduit distributing left ventricular stroke volume.
structures.clinicalRelevance: Abdominal aortic aneurysm rupture presents with hypotension and flank pain.
